findings.title: Mouse clicks fail on multiple primary controls due pointer interception
findings.severity_rationale: Primary booking and account-entry actions are not operable by standard mouse click across multiple pages.
findings.impact: Mouse users may be blocked from login, navigation, reservation continuation, and cancellation actions.
preconditions: Any page with target controls visible
steps: Open home page and click `Saved stays` in header
Open login page and click `Continue as demo guest`
Open hotel detail and click `Continue to reservation`
findings.expected: Each visible link/button should activate on mouse click.
findings.expected_basis: Standard web interaction model and UI affordances.
findings.actual: Click attempts timed out repeatedly; overlapping container elements intercepted pointer events.
findings.comparison: Keyboard focus + Enter succeeded for the same controls in several cases.
findings.recommendation: Review stacking context and pointer-events behavior for interactive controls and overlapping containers; add E2E checks for click hit-target integrity.

findings.title: `Price: low to high` does not produce ascending order
findings.severity_rationale: Users can still browse properties, but pricing sort order is materially misleading for decision-making.
findings.impact: Users may select more expensive stays first despite requesting ascending price sort.
preconditions: On discover page with list visible
Pool filter active during sampled run
steps: Set sort to `Price: low to high`
Review visible nightly prices from top to bottom
findings.expected: Visible order should be ascending by numeric nightly rate.
findings.expected_basis: Sort option label and common booking UX semantics.
findings.actual: Observed ordering was not ascending (e.g., RM 890 before RM 680 and RM 780).
findings.recommendation: Validate sort comparator and ensure numeric normalization before ordering rendered cards.
